page.layout: One page of text, one column. Heading block at the top (work title, centred, over several lines), then two verse stanzas with the second headed "EIDEM.". Catchword "Nec" at the lower right.

l.i: DVM quasint[?] morbis medicamina certa,
MO-NAVI,
Sedulus inquiris, metuens Mors ipsa, morari
Saeuitiam ipsum ne posses arte reperta,
Seruandis intentum aliis, vitaque tuenda
Immemorem propria te funere mersit acerbo.
Sed quid si potius sese Mors ipsa fefellit?
Suetus enim morbos non Mortem vincere vivus,
Vita nunc vera sancte[?] moriendo potitus
Quadam etiam Mortem docuisti morte domari.
EIDEM.
Si qui nunc tacet hoc iacens sepulchro,
Aut ipsum queat hoc loqui sepulchrum,
Eius nomine quem tegit sepultum,
Audires subito tuas, viator,
Qui linguis tribus insonans ad aures,
Te quotcunque, tribusve, pluribusve
Sunt recte utiliterque scripta linguis,
Argute, solideque perdoceret.
Sed quum neque queat hoc loqui sepulchrum,

page.notes: The first word "DVM" carries a large woodcut-style initial D; the first line reads "quasint" (possibly quaesint), marked [?]. In "ipsium" a small superscript s sits above the line. "sancte" is a doubtful ligature, marked [?]. In the last verse line a superscript "non" is printed above "neque" as a correction; I have kept "neque queat" as the main reading. The small dash at the right beside "Argute" is a printer's mark, not text. "Nec" at the lower right is the catchword.
